item.title: Self-Hosted GPIO Web Control Dashboards: pigpiod vs gpiozero vs libgpiod
item.description: General Purpose Input/Output (GPIO) pins are the bridge between software and the physical world. Whether you’re controlling relays, reading sensors, driving motors, or blinking LEDs, your application needs a reliable way to talk to GPIO hardware. When that control needs to happen over a network — a web dashboard toggling lights, a monitoring system reading temperature sensors, or a test automation framework manipulating hardware — you need a GPIO server that exposes pins through a network-accessible API. Three Linux-based open-source frameworks — pigpiod, gpiozero, and libgpiod — each take a different approach to this challenge.
